chunks: The day they see the angels, there will be no happy tidings for the sinners; and they will say: 'There is an insurmountable barrier!'
ai.seo_question: What do the sinners say when they see the angels on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the finality of divine decree, where the sight of angels—typically bearers of good news—becomes a source of dread for the *Mujrimin* due to their accumulated sins. The phrase 'Hijran Mahjuran' (a sealed barrier) is interpreted not merely as a physical wall but as a spiritual closure of the heart, preventing them from accepting mercy or entering Paradise. This reflects the principle that the consequences of one's actions create an insurmountable distance from the divine presence on the Day of Resurrection.
